record.paper_title: Progress and open questions in the physics of neutrino cross sections at intermediate energies
record.original_question: Can improved measurements of pion absorption and pion charge-exchange cross sections in nuclei reduce the present uncertainty in neutrino-induced pion final-state-interaction models enough to resolve the discrepancies between theory and experiment in nuclear pion production?

evidence.quote: In this respect, the DUET experiment at TRIUMF, that uses the PIAνO detector [220], will provide quite valuable information in the future.
The objective of the experiment is to measure π absorption and π charge exchange cross section with ∼ 10% and ∼ 20% accuracy, respectively.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider neutrino-induced pion production on a complex nucleus, in which a pion produced at a primary interaction vertex (e.g., via resonance excitation or coherent production) propagates through the residual nuclear medium and undergoes final-state interactions (FSI). The dominant FSI channels are: (i) elastic and quasi-elastic pion-nucleon scattering, (ii) pion absorption (in which the pion is absorbed on a correlated nucleon pair, leaving no pion in the final state), and (iii) single charge exchange (π± → π0 or π0 → π±). Models of pion FSI in nuclei (typically based on intranuclear cascade or quantum-mechanical Δ-hole approaches) take, as inputs, energy-dependent cross sections σ_abs(T_π, A) and σ_cex(T_π, A) for pion absorption and charge exchange on nuclei of mass number A. Existing discrepancies between measured and predicted exclusive nuclear pion-production yields (in particular for charged-current single-pion production on carbon and oxygen targets at neutrino energies of order 1 GeV) are partly attributed to uncertainties in these FSI inputs.

Question: Suppose new measurements determine σ_abs(T_π, A) on relevant nuclei (e.g., carbon) to a relative accuracy of approximately 10% and σ_cex(T_π, A) to approximately 20% over the kinematically relevant pion kinetic-energy range (roughly 100–400 MeV). Using these inputs to constrain pion-FSI models, can the resulting reduction in the FSI systematic uncertainty be made small enough to bring theoretical predictions of nuclear pion-production cross sections into quantitative agreement with the existing experimental measurements?
artifact.category_tag: neutrino-nucleus cross sections and pion final-state interactions
artifact.status_search_result: The DUET experiment at TRIUMF subsequently published measurements of π+ absorption and charge exchange on carbon (arXiv:1506.07783), reducing the relevant FSI parameter uncertainties by roughly a factor of two compared to earlier data. These measurements have been incorporated as constraints in pion-FSI/intranuclear-cascade models used by T2K and similar experiments, leading to a substantial reduction of FSI systematic uncertainties. However, residual tensions between theoretical predictions and measurements of neutrino-induced nuclear pion production persist, so the broader question of fully resolving the theory–experiment discrepancy is only partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of absorption and charge exchange of π+ on carbon (DUET)
status_evidence.snippet: DUET measured the combined absorption and charge exchange cross sections of π+ on carbon in the 200–300 MeV/c range with uncertainties reduced by roughly half compared to previous experiments.
status_evidence.claim: Improved measurements of pion absorption and charge exchange on carbon were performed and reduced relevant uncertainties significantly.

status_evidence.title: Pion Scattering Measurements – NuSTEC Pion Workshop 2019
status_evidence.snippet: DUET measurements are used to constrain pion FSI models in neutrino generators, reducing FSI systematic uncertainties; remaining discrepancies in neutrino pion production motivate further measurements.
status_evidence.claim: DUET-type measurements have improved FSI constraints but discrepancies in neutrino pion production are not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Using world charged pion–nucleus scattering data to constrain an intranuclear cascade model
status_evidence.snippet: Combined fits to pion-nucleus scattering data including DUET reduce uncertainties in INC FSI parameters used to model neutrino interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Pion-nucleus data including DUET have been used to reduce FSI parameter uncertainties in models, but theory–experiment tension in neutrino pion production remains.
